subject: Genetics
title: High-Altitude Adaptation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on High-Altitude Adaptation.

hook.text: At 4,000 meters, oxygen drops 40%. Most people get altitude sickness. Tibetans thrive there effortlessly.

buildup.text: Tibetans have a variant of the EPAS1 gene that prevents overproduction of red blood cells at altitude.

discovery.text: Too many red cells thicken blood, causing strokes. Tibetans avoid this. Their blood stays fluid at extreme heights.

twist.text: The EPAS1 variant came from Denisovans—an extinct human species. Tibetans inherited it through interbreeding.

climax.text: Andean people adapted differently—with larger lungs and more hemoglobin. Same problem, two genetic solutions.

punchline.text: An extinct species gave Tibetans the genes to breathe at the roof of the world.

quiz.question: Where did the Tibetan EPAS1 variant come from?
